tagline: Hand off or compact, keeping what you pick

cost.summary: No background model call by default. Turn on `Automatic handoff` and Sonnet updates the handoff after each turn; Haiku reads the threads when the card opens (`Read the threads`).
readme: Automatic handoff is off by default. With it off, the mod makes no background model call: nothing runs after a turn or after a /clear. The two calls that remain start only when you open or use the Wrap up card.
Turn Automatic handoff on (`/mod-wrap-up settings`) and the mod calls a model in more places, which spends tokens and counts against your plan quota.

| After each turn (or every few turns, set by Update every (turns)), the automatic handoff updates the ledger and handoff from the turns since the last update, up to 150,000 characters | Sonnet at low effort | Automatic handoff off (the default) |
| The first prompt after a /clear that is not a slash command, a "related?" check against the ledger | Sonnet at low effort, a reply of at most 100 tokens | Automatic handoff off (the default) |
| Opening the Wrap up card splits the session into threads | Haiku | Read the threads off |
| Handoff in the card writes the summary | Your session's model through a fork; Sonnet when there is nothing to fork yet | Does not run unless you click it |

The Sonnet calls are pinned to Sonnet. When Sonnet is blocked or unavailable for you (the call is refused, or answers forbidden or not found), the mod retries once with your session's model, so it spends that model's tokens instead.

With Auto handoff at the mark on, the countdown first runs one more ledger update if turns are waiting. Set Automatic handoff to off and only the Wrap up pill hands off. Change settings with `/mod-wrap-up settings`.

The ledger holds the handoff text. It is one JSON file per session chain, written under `~/.claude/mods-data/mod-wrap-up/chains/`. When `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is set, the folder is `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/mods-data/mod-wrap-up/` instead. The mod never prunes these files, so delete old ones by hand.

features.title: Pick what stays
features.detail: A click on Wrap up offers Handoff or Compact. Either opens a card with the session's threads, read by Haiku, and fixed items such as files in play and open tasks; a click keeps or drops each line. The Auto switch beside them turns the auto handoff on or off, and its tip says what is set now.

features.title: Compact
features.detail: The card writes the /compact instructions as you click and Fill prompt puts them in the prompt. You review them and press Enter.

features.title: Handoff
features.detail: Summarizes what stays through a hidden fork, runs /clear, and fills the handoff into the fresh prompt.

features.title: Session names
features.detail: The card proposes a /rename for the session you leave and one for the fresh session. A click keeps or skips each. The names link as `previous <- next`, with one arrow. A name you wrote yourself is kept and linked, never replaced.

features.title: Carried card
features.detail: After a carried /clear a card shows `previous <- current` and the goal that came along. Show all grows a long goal to its full text, and Show less cuts it to one line. Start fresh drops the carried handoff and starts a new ledger; the earlier one stays on disk.

features.title: Automatic handoff
features.detail: After each turn Sonnet keeps a ledger of decisions and tasks, plus a fresh handoff, in the background. /compact is given the handoff and the next prompt carries it. With Auto handoff at the mark on, a card counts down 5 seconds between turns at 400K tokens or 65% of the window, whichever comes first; Cancel, a typed draft or a new turn stops it. At zero the ledger is brought up to date and the chat is cleared. If the ledger has an open task, Claude continues it from the handoff; otherwise the handoff is filled into the prompt and nothing is sent. After /clear, a related first prompt carries it and an unrelated one starts a new ledger; a card offers a switch. Each session keeps its own ledger, so sessions in one folder never mix.

features.title: Command hooks
features.detail: On SessionStart (including the one after a compact), a small shell hook appends the event's JSON as one line to `~/.claude/mods-data/mod-wrap-up/bridge/<session id>.jsonl` (under `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when that is set), and the mod reads the file every 250 ms. A record can hold the session id, the working folder and the transcript path. SessionEnd deletes the session's file, and SessionStart deletes files older than 7 days. The hooks need a POSIX shell (Git Bash on Windows). Without one they write nothing, and the mod falls back to what it can find on its own. Some plans block plugin hooks on these events; the mod then falls back the same way.
